# Unique usernames

Implement `Registry` in `solution.py`, keeping all state in `runtime.Store` (see
`runtime.py`). Each user holds at most one name, and each name belongs to at most one
user.

```python
Registry(store)
register(user: str, name: str) -> bool
rename(user: str, new_name: str) -> bool
owner(name: str) -> str | None
name_of(user: str) -> str | None
```

- Names are 1 to 16 characters from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, compared case-insensitively:
  `Bob` and `bob` are the same name. Store and return names in lower case. Calls with
  an invalid name return `False` (or `None` for `owner`) and change nothing.
- `register` gives `user` the name if the user has no name and nobody holds the name.
  Registering the name the user already holds returns `True`. Otherwise `False`.
- `rename` moves a user who holds a name to `new_name` if nobody else holds it; the
  old name becomes free. Renaming to the name the user already holds returns `True`.
  On `False`, nothing changes.
- `owner` and `name_of` return the current holder and name.
- Many `Registry` objects in many threads may share one `Store`. Calls for the same
  user never overlap; calls for different users may. When no call is in progress,
  `owner(n) == u` exactly when `name_of(u) == n`.

Use P to model the design before implementing it, and to test the implementation.
`snappea` and the `pysnappea` Python package are installed. Keep your P files and
tests in this directory; the tests must run with `python -m pytest`.
----
---
name: p-modeling
description: Design concurrent or retrying code with a P model checked by snappea, then test the real implementation against what the model found.
---

# P modeling

P finds bugs that only appear in some orderings: two clients read the same version,
a retry arrives after the state changed, a step fails between read and write. Use it
for shared state, retries, concurrency and recovery. Pure transformations need only
ordinary tests.

The model is worth what it changes in the code and tests. Follow these steps in order.
The same steps are built into the CLI: `snappea guide`.

## 1. List the risks (before any code)

Write down, in `DESIGN.md`:

- the contract in checkable sentences ("a retried request returns its first result and
  has no further effect");
- the real atomic primitives (one compare-and-swap on one key, a lock, a transaction).
  Everything else can interleave;
- 5-10 concrete scenarios that could break the contract. Always consider:
  two clients that read the same version; a retry after another request changed the
  state (including retries of rejected or empty results); two objects sharing one
  store; each precondition false on its own; values exactly at each boundary.

## 2. Model the algorithm, not the API

- One machine for the store, holding exactly what the real store holds. Its handlers
  are the real primitives: `load` replies with (version, value); `cas` succeeds only at
  the current version.
- Client machines run your algorithm: send load, receive, decide, send cas, retry on
  failure. Every `send`/`receive` is a point where another client can run. If the
  whole operation is one handler, the model assumes the race away.
- A `spec` monitor computes the expected results from the contract and the history of
  requests, independently of the algorithm, and asserts each actual result.
- Drive it with 2-3 clients and small `choose(n)` inputs, plus fixed tests for the
  scenarios from step 1. Start from the [syntax reference](reference/p-patterns.md)
  and [CAS + retries example](examples/cas-retry/Balance.p).

## 3. Check until it passes for real

```sh
snappea check            # every test case, then coverage and mutation checks
```

- Exit 1 is work to do: a bug (fix the design; keep the scenario), a coverage gap
  (add a scenario), or a surviving mutant (an assertion is missing). Read each one.
- Do not finish with `--no-mutation` or `--allow-incomplete-coverage`. Use them only
  while iterating. If search is incomplete, shrink the bounds or raise `--timeout`.
- A bug found here is the payoff: write it down, fix the design, then implement.

## 4. Implement, then test what the model explored

Read [testing the implementation](guides/testing-implementation.md). For each
scenario and each bug the model found, write a Python test that makes it happen on the
real code. Random thread stress rarely hits a race; force it:

- wrap the store so a competing call runs between this call's load and its
  compare-and-swap, or so two calls read the same version before either writes;
- retry a request after another request changed the state, through a second object.

Add an observation test: run real calls, record their actual arguments and results as
events, and check them against your P spec with `snappea.check_events` (install
`pysnappea`, `import snappea`). See [implementation](guides/implementation.md).

## 5. Prove the tests can fail

Break your implementation on purpose, one change at a time (ignore the
compare-and-swap result, drop a retry memo, flip a boundary `<` to `<=`, keep state
in the object instead of the store). Run the tests each time; every break must fail a
test. Add a test for any that pass. Restore the code.

## Done means

- `snappea check` exits 0, with complete search or stated bounds.
- `python -m pytest` passes, including forced-interleaving and observation tests.
- Every hand-made break from step 5 fails a test.
- `DESIGN.md` states the contract, primitives, scenarios, model bounds, what the model
  found, and what is not covered.

## References

- [Syntax and commands](reference/p-patterns.md), [modeling](guides/modeling.md),
  [scenarios and oracles](guides/scenarios-and-oracles.md), [recovery](guides/recovery.md).
- Examples: [CAS + generated retries](examples/cas-retry/Balance.p),
  [reservation + Python tests](examples/reservation/Reservation.p),
  [generated histories](examples/bounded-history/bounded-history.p),
  [durable retry](examples/durable-retry/DurableRetry.p),
  [versioned publication](examples/versioned-publication/Revalidated.p).

🫛 snappea checks P models.

Usage: snappea [output options] <command> [options]

Commands:
  check      Find bugs in a model: run its test cases over many schedules.
             Use after every model change.
  replay     Re-run a bug's .schedule file to debug it or confirm a fix
  tests      List test cases, e.g. to pick one for `check`
  observe    Check logs of a real system against the model's spec monitors.
             Use to test that an implementation matches the model.
  coverage   Merge coverage from several runs (CI shards, processes)
  guide      How to model a design and test code against it. Start here:
             `snappea guide`, then `snappea guide testing` or `snappea guide syntax`.
  version    Print the version

Typical loop:
  snappea check                       # check every test case
  snappea replay PCheckerOutput/tcFoo/bug.schedule -v   # debug a bug
  snappea check tcFoo                 # confirm the fix

Commands that read P sources take .pproj or .p files. Without any, they use the
*.pproj file in the current folder, or else the *.p files in it and its immediate
subfolders.

Output is text on a terminal or in CI, JSON otherwise (agents, scripts).
--format text|json, --json or SNAPPEA_FORMAT=text|json override it.
--json-report FILE also writes the JSON result to FILE.

Run `snappea <command> --help` for a command's options and examples.
Usage: snappea guide [TOPIC]

Prints a short guide, as Markdown. Topics:
  workflow   (default) Model the design, check it, then test the code against it
  testing    Force the interleavings the model found in implementation tests, and check
             real calls against the P spec
  syntax     P syntax and a complete small model

Example:

"""Forced interleavings from the P model (Names.p), validation, and observation."""
import random
import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import pytest
from snappea import check_events

from runtime import Store
from solution import Registry


class HookStore:
    """Real store with hooks run around load/compare_swap on chosen keys."""

    def __init__(self, inner=None):
        self.inner = inner or Store()
        self.after_load = None   # f(key) called after a load returns
        self.before_cas = None   # f(key, value) called before a CAS
        self.log = []            # (key, old_value, new_value) of successful CAS

    def load(self, key):
        result = self.inner.load(key)
        hook = self.after_load
        if hook:
            hook(key)
        return result

    def compare_swap(self, key, version, value):
        hook = self.before_cas
        if hook:
            hook(key, value)
        old = self.inner.load(key)[1]
        ok = self.inner.compare_swap(key, version, value)
        if ok:
            self.log.append((key, old, value))
        return ok


def once(fn):
    done = []

    def run(*a):
        if not done:
            done.append(1)
            fn(*a)
    return run


def consistent(store, users, names):
    """owner(n) == u exactly when name_of(u) == n."""
    r = Registry(store)
    for n in names:
        for u in users:
            assert (r.owner(n) == u) == (r.name_of(u) == n), (n, u)


# ---- validation -----------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", ["", "a" * 17, "a b", "a_b", "é", "a\n", "K", "A!", " ", None, 5])
def test_invalid_names_change_nothing(bad):
    store = Store()
    r = Registry(store)
    assert r.register("u", "ok") is True
    assert r.register("v", bad) is False
    assert r.rename("u", bad) is False
    assert r.owner(bad) is None
    assert r.name_of("v") is None and r.name_of("u") == "ok" and r.owner("ok") == "u"


def test_length_boundaries_and_charset():
    r = Registry(Store())
    assert r.register("a", "x") is True            # 1
    assert r.register("b", "a" * 16) is True       # 16
    assert r.register("c", "a" * 17) is False      # 17
    assert r.register("d", "0-9-z") is True
    assert r.owner("A" * 16) == "b"
    assert r.name_of("b") == "a" * 16


def test_case_insensitive_and_lowercase_storage():
    r = Registry(Store())
    assert r.register("u", "Bob") is True
    assert r.name_of("u") == "bob" and r.owner("BOB") == "u"
    assert r.register("v", "bOb") is False
    assert r.register("u", "BOB") is True
    assert r.register("u", "other") is False
    assert r.rename("u", "BoB") is True
    assert r.rename("u", "Carl") is True
    assert r.owner("bob") is None and r.name_of("u") == "carl"
    assert r.register("v", "bob") is True


# ---- sequential contract -----------------------------------------------------

def test_each_precondition_alone():
    r = Registry(Store())
    assert r.rename("u", "a") is False               # no name yet
    assert r.name_of("u") is None and r.owner("a") is None
    assert r.register("u", "a") is True
    assert r.register("u", "b") is False             # user has a name
    assert r.register("v", "a") is False             # name taken
    assert r.rename("v", "b") is False               # v has no name
    assert r.register("v", "b") is True
    assert r.rename("v", "a") is False               # taken by u; v keeps b
    assert r.name_of("v") == "b" and r.owner("b") == "v" and r.owner("a") == "u"
    assert r.rename("v", "b") is True
    assert r.rename("u", "c") is True
    assert r.register("w", "a") is True              # old name is free
    consistent(r._store, ["u", "v", "w"], ["a", "b", "c"])


# ---- forced interleavings ----------------------------------------------------

def test_two_users_read_same_free_name_one_wins():
    inner = Store()
    barrier = threading.Barrier(2, timeout=3)
    store = HookStore(inner)
    store.after_load = lambda key: barrier.wait() if key == "name:x" else None
    a, b = Registry(store), Registry(store)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as pool:
        fa, fb = pool.submit(a.register, "ua", "x"), pool.submit(b.register, "ub", "x")
        results = sorted([fa.result(5), fb.result(5)])
    store.after_load = None
    assert results == [False, True]
    consistent(inner, ["ua", "ub"], ["x"])
    winner = a.owner("x")
    assert winner in ("ua", "ub") and a.name_of(winner) == "x"
    loser = "ub" if winner == "ua" else "ua"
    assert a.name_of(loser) is None


def test_competitor_between_load_and_cas_forces_reject():
    store = HookStore()
    r = Registry(store)
    rival = Registry(store.inner)

    rival = Registry(store.inner)

    rng = random.Random(7)
    inner = Store()
    users = [f"u{i}" for i in range(6)]
    names = [f"n{i}" for i in range(4)]
    plans = {u: [(rng.choice(["register", "rename"]), rng.choice(names)) for _ in range(40)] for u in users}

    def run(u):
        r = Registry(inner)
        for op, n in plans[u]:
            getattr(r, op)(u, n)

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(len(users)) as pool:

# ---- observation against the P spec ---------------------------------------------

IDS = {"u1": 1, "u2": 2, "a": 3, "b": 4, "c": 5, "d": 6}


class Observed:
    """Records actual calls, the store's name transitions, and the final state as
    events for the Contract monitor in Names.p."""

    def __init__(self, contended):
        self.store = HookStore()
        self.reg = Registry(self.store)
        self.events = []
        self.contended = contended
        self.seen = 0

    def _flush_holds(self):
        for key, old, new in self.store.log[self.seen:]:
            if key.startswith("name:"):
                self.events.append({"event": "eHold", "payload": {
                    "name": IDS[key[5:]], "before": IDS[old] if old else 0, "after": IDS[new] if new else 0}})
        self.seen = len(self.store.log)

    def call(self, op, user, name):
        ok = getattr(self.reg, op)(user, name)
        self._flush_holds()
        self.events.append({"event": "eReturned", "payload": {
            "user": IDS[user], "isRegister": op == "register", "name": IDS[name],
            "ok": ok, "contended": self.contended}})
        return ok

    def check(self):
        names, users = {}, {}
        for n in ("a", "b", "c", "d"):
            holder = self.reg.owner(n)
            if self.store.inner.load("name:" + n)[0]:
                names[IDS[n]] = IDS[holder] if holder else 0
        for u in ("u1", "u2"):
            name = self.reg.name_of(u)
            if self.store.inner.load("user:" + u)[0]:
                users[IDS[u]] = IDS[name] if name else 0
        self.events.append({"event": "eFinal", "payload": {"names": names, "users": users}})
        check_events(self.events, "Contract", spec_files=["Names.p"], strict=True, unknown_events="error")


def test_observed_sequence_matches_spec():
    o = Observed(contended=False)
    assert o.call("register", "u1", "a") is True
    assert o.call("rename", "u1", "c") is True
    assert o.call("register", "u2", "a") is True
    assert o.call("rename", "u2", "d") is True
    o.check()


def test_observed_contention_matches_spec():
    o = Observed(contended=True)
    assert o.call("register", "u1", "a") is True
    assert o.call("register", "u2", "a") is False
    assert o.call("rename", "u2", "b") is False
    assert o.call("register", "u2", "b") is True
    o.check()


def test_observation_rejects_a_wrong_history():
    o = Observed(contended=True)
    o.call("register", "u1", "a")
    o.call("register", "u2", "a")
    o.call("rename", "u2", "b")
    o.call("register", "u2", "b")
    o.events[-1]["payload"]["ok"] = False   # claim a wrong result
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        o.check()

# Unique usernames: design

## Contract
- Names: 1-16 chars of `a-z0-9-`, case-insensitive, stored lower case. Invalid name: `False`/`None`, no change.
- `register`: succeeds if the user has no name and nobody holds the name; re-registering the held name is `True`.
- `rename`: only for a user with a name; succeeds if nobody else holds the new name, frees the old; same name is `True`.
- Quiescent invariant: `owner(n) == u` exactly when `name_of(u) == n`.

## Primitives
Per key atomic `load` and `compare_swap`; no cross-key transaction. Calls for one user never overlap.
Keys: `name:<n>` -> user, `user:<u>` -> name (`None` = free / none).

## Algorithm
- `register`: load `user:u`; decide from it; claim `name:n` with one CAS from free; then write `user:u`.
- `rename`: load `user:u`; claim the new `name:n`; write `user:u`; release old `name:o` by CAS to free.
  The name CAS is the only contested step; the user record and the held old name have a single writer, so those writes cannot lose (the model asserts it).
- While a rename is in flight the user holds both names; another user registering the old name then fails (it is linearized before the rename). Quiescent state is consistent.

## Scenarios (Names.p, 8 tests, all searched completely)
two users read the same free name (one CAS loses); same user re-registering; swap renames (A->y while B->x);
disjoint users must always succeed; rename to the held name; rename with no name; second user takes a name
freed by a completed rename; generated names for two users with register+rename and register+register.

## Model bounds and oracle
2 users, 2 ops each, names 3..4 (plus fixed scenarios with up to 6), 1000s of schedules, exhaustive.
`Contract` spec: transitions of each name go from the current holder; per-user results follow the user's own last
success; uncontended or sequential operations must succeed; final state is consistent both ways and equals the
announced transitions and last successes.

## What the model found
No bug in the final design. The first coverage/mutation runs showed gaps (no scenario for a nameless rename, rename
to the same name, name ids overlapping user ids, versions not asserted to increase); each was fixed with a scenario or assertion.
A design note: a failed register of a name whose rename-away is in flight is allowed (linearized earlier), so the spec
only demands success when no other call is in flight (sequential or disjoint names).

## Python tests (test_solution.py)
Forced interleavings (same free name read by two; competitor between load and CAS for register and rename; rival
between claim and release), second object on same store, validation boundaries, thread stress, and observation tests
using `check_events` with `Contract`. Hand-made breaks (ignore CAS result, skip load, no release, release first,
flip each precondition/boundary, state in object, wrong key, etc.) all fail a test, except lowercase-before-regex
(equivalent: `A-Z` in the regex is harmless).

## Not covered
Crashes between steps (a crash after claim leaves a name held with no user record), more than two users or ops,
real-concurrency linearizability beyond the model, observation of concurrent returns (only sequential orderings).
EOF
